# Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet On-Ear Active Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones – Lightweight Headphones for Kids – Safer Sound Studio-Grade Quality
Brand: Puro Sound Labs
Category: Headphones & Earbuds > On-Ear Headphones

## Features
ACTIVE NOISE-CANCELLING HEADPHONES The ANC switch puts the world on mute so that kids can listen clearly in loud environments.These headphones make daily noise and background sounds up to 22 dB quieter, complemented by 82% noise isolation (@ 1 KHz).; LIMITED VOLUME FOR KIDS’ HEARING SAFETY A limited volume of 85 dB is the maximum safe sound listening level as recommended by many organizations. Intelligent digital signal processing imperceptibly limits the volume so that listeners don’t even notice.; WIRELESS HEADPHONES WITH BLUETOOTH FUNCTION The one-touch Bluetooth pairing with iPhone, Android, and other compatible devices makes for hassle-free listening! The wireless mode eliminates all dangers of entanglement in audio cables.; LONG BATTERY LIFE Enjoy up to 22 hours of non-ANC play time (16 hours with ANC) and 200 hours of standby. Quickly recharge the lithium-ion battery with included USB cable or switch to wired use with the included volume limiting audio cable.; 30-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE The warranty period for our products is 1 full year. If you have an issue with one of our products, we maintain a 30-day money-back guarantee. It’s as simple as that!

## Specifications
Color: Blue; Enclosure Material: Aluminum; Additional Features: Foldable, Lightweight, Microphone Included, Noise Cancellation, Noise Isolation, Volume Control; Built-In Media: Cable, Hard Cover travel case, Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet headphones, USB charging cable; Age Range Description: Kid

## Pricing & Reviews
Rated 4.4 from 272 reviews.
Top review: We have had two sets of these headphones for about 18 months. My two school-aged children have used them on planes, trains, and automobiles and they have been a worthwhile investment. As a musician, it's important to me to preserve my children's hearing, and I was concerned at how high they were turning up the volume on their music/games/programs when we traveled. That concern has only widened as we've moved to more and more virtual learning and gatherings this year. I love that these headphones, which are sleek, sturdy, and good looking, limit the volume to a reasonable level, particularly for their age. I also appreciate that each pair came with its own hard case, to keep them safe and tidy. I did have an issue with one set of headphones, but I reached out to Puro's customer service team and they went above and beyond to resolve the issue quickly and to my satisfaction. I would definitely buy from them again.

## Details
Model: PQBLU. UPC: 854381006386

## Description
Hello, healthy ears! Puro Sound Labs’ lightweight headphones for boys, girls and teens are a safer sound solution for your child’s hearing, and the sound is terrifically crisp! Our Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Kids’ Wireless Headphones promote healthy ears by limiting the volume to 85 dB (the maximum safe listening level as recommended by many organizations, including the Hearing Health Foundation, OSHA, and the World Health Foundation) and blocking out 82% of the background noise. Our design features active and passive noise isolation and is able to block background noise on a level that is comparable to some of the best active noise-cancelling headphones on the market. Enjoy up to 22 hours of play time and 16 hours with ANC (Active Noise Cancellation Function). A volume limiting cable compatible with non-Bluetooth devices is also included for continuous use in case the battery dies. The super-soft vegan leather-wrapped headband and ear cushions ensure long wearing comfort, combined with a smooth sliding arm so that boys, girls and teens can adjust the headphones to suit their head sizes and shapes. Its AL6063 aluminum body enhances durability to withstand rough play, and the lightweight construction, only weighing around 169g, creates almost no pressure on young heads! The purchase of our product also includes a USB charging cable, a volume limiting 3.5mm audio cable, a hard cover travel case, and a user manual. Taking advantage of PuroQuiet ANC technology, 85 dB volume limiting, and 82% noise isolation, kids can listen to true-to-life audio without the need to volume up in noisy environments, reducing the risk of noise-induced hearing loss or partial deafness.

If you’re a new parent or someone unlucky enough to have a small head, finding headphones can be a huge pain in the neck. That’s where the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet comes in. This is one of the most credible Bluetooth headsets for smaller heads out there, and it’s a good set of ANC headphones to boot. I strongly recommend this headset for younger listeners, as it helps them avoid the temptation to give themselves noise-induced hearing loss.

Editor’s note: this PuroQuiet review was updated on November 23, 2020, to mention the PuroGamer gaming headset.

## Who are the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet for?

Smaller earpads mean better fit for littler ears.

Listeners who have smaller heads or are younger will appreciate the option for active noise canceling on smaller ears. Older listeners, teenagers, and those with larger heads will probably not find the fit to work all that well.

## What’s it like to use the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet?

While I can’t tell you exactly what it’s like because I’m a 33 year-old man, I can tell you that the Puro PuroQuiet ANC headphones do a great job of fitting smaller heads. Until receiving a loan unit from Puro Labs, we had been using larger ear protection for my daughter, but the loose fit and heat buildup meant she’d usually toss them off her head after about 20 minutes if she didn’t fall asleep. I’m not going to pretend that “adult-size” tools will ever really be suited for smaller bodies—but there really is a dearth of good items for the people who need it the most.

The Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet ANC headphones represent a solid effort into reaching these customers who are often overlooked. Making kids’ products isn’t sexy; it isn’t a good way to make a popular product simply because the design process is extremely difficult, and customers don’t want to commit to investing in something that will only last a short time. I swear and grumble every single time that expensive baby item gets too small or stops working.

The Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet can use a 3.5mm cable when the battery runs out, and charges with a microUSB.

If you have an old phone charger (microUSB) lying around, you can repurpose it to charge these headphones. Once full, use the switches on the back to turn on the wireless connection, and the noise canceling if you’d like to use it with or without music. You’ll have to set up the pairing if it’s your first time using the headphones with your phone, but the headphones will then remember the device every time after that. You can then walk up to 10 meters from your phone or laptop when using the headset.

## Why would you buy the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet?

The PuroQuiet ANC headphones are a good choice if you’re looking for headphones instead of merely protecting your smaller ears. They are built for safe music listening, not a primary means of hearing protection. For that, you’d want something like a set of ear protectors or earplugs.

The buttons are chunky and easy to find on the back of the earcup.

By offering an ANC option for younger listeners that isn’t steeped in an obviously “for kids” design aesthetic, the PuroQuiet accomplishes three things:

1. Offers your children and young adults a set of headphones they’ll actually use
2. Prevents noise induced hearing loss by capping the sound pressure level output at 85dB
3. Reduces the overall volume level they’ll choose by attenuating outside noise

This is very similar to any set of noise-canceling headphones, but with the addition of a volume limiter. By combining these approaches, you set a reasonable set of guardrails for your young listener—so they’re very unlikely to damage their hearing unintentionally by listening to music on the bus or train. I say unlikely because it’s still possible; but by making sure there isn’t much of a reason to crank the volume (noise canceling coupled with the hard volume limit), you disincentivize loud listening.

Additionally, by preventing high doses of sound pressure on young ears: you prevent your listener from losing hearing in higher frequencies too early.

## What do the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet headphones sound like?

For the most part, the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet has notably good sound quality, save for the normal headaches associated with Bluetooth. The only reason I mention that is because to a younger listener, the sound quality will be slightly decreased despite most people being unable to tell the difference. It’s an age thing—after you pass your mid-twenties, you’re able to hear less and less high-frequency sound, so it’s something to be aware of. I maintain the freedom from wires is essential for younger listeners, and not every 6 year old is a concert pianist.

Although the bass is boosted just a little bit, most of the notes will come through as they’re supposed to.

Bass notes (pink) will be nudged up a little, as well as mids (green), but overall most music will sound as its supposed to. There isn’t a high level of noise, and users of the PuroQuiet won’t have to suffer at the hands of extreme emphasis in the high notes like some headphones do. If there’s complaints about lack of bass: it might just be the fit of the headphones, but it could also be that it’s not what your listener is used to.

## How good is the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet’s noise canceling?

That ANC switch is easy to toggle.

To be perfectly honest, the noise cancellation properties of the PuroQuiet are pretty standard. But “standard” ANC in this day and age is pretty damned good.

The Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet blocks out a considerable amount of low-frequency noise, which is great for the bus or train.

This headset does an exceptional job at keeping low sounds like engine noise and the rumble of rail transportation down to about half or one third as loud as they would be without any headphones on. While that may not seem like much, it’s a significant reduction in the force applied to your ears. However, ANC headsets don’t block out all sound, primarily just continuous noise. Incidental noise like clapping, people talking, and street noise will cut right through, though it won’t be quite as loud.

## How good is the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet’s battery?

If you’re using the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet on an airplane, a single charge will last you roughly 12 hours and 35 minutes—so unless you’re flying across the globe you should be fine for a one-way trip. That’s with both the music blasting at 75dB and the ANC turned on. Obviously your mileage will vary based on how loud you listen to these headphones, or if you use the ANC. This figure is merely a performance floor.

I will point out that several other headsets including the Bose QuietComfort 35 II, Sony WH-1000XM4, and Shure AONIC 50 all have about double the battery life. If you can fit into one of those, I will always recommend those over the PuroQuiet. Unfortunately, those are all over three times the cost as the PuroQuiet—so you’re a better judge as to what suits your individual needs here.

...a single charge will last you roughly 12 hours and 35 minutes

However, if you do run out of battery, you can use the included 3.5mm to 3.5mm wire to plug the headphones into the headphone jack of any source that supports it. If you have a phone without a headphone jack, the battery running out means the end of your listening.

## Should you buy the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet headphones?

I’m torn on whether or not to recommend these headphones, because it rests entirely on whether or not they can fit around their user’s ear. If they can’t, then their ANC performance is fairly pedestrian, and you may be better off simply buying a larger set. However, these headphones work as advertised: they are excellent ANC headphones for smaller heads and ears.

I will say I’m very happy that these headphones don’t lean into a kid-centric aesthetic, because that sort of thing isn’t always appropriate for the potential audience of these headphones. Adults with small heads do exist, and it’s cool that something can serve many audiences without telegraphing an assumed user type. It can be demeaning.

The Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet represent a very solid attempt at ANC for younger listeners without assuming that their listeners won’t care about audio quality or isolation. They may not be for everyone, but they are a great option for a lot of people. Just be sure they’ll fit the head of your intended user before buying.

# 1 Honest Puro PuroQuiet Noise Cancelling Headphones Review

 10:37 AM 

Today I”m sharing our honest PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review. If you read my blog regularly, you’ll know we are a pretty geeky family. The kids both love their tech, but aren’t fans of excessive noise. Now that Syd is home schooling, it’s been a challenge getting her to focus on the task at hand when there’s so many distractions at home. So when Puro got in touch and asked me to do a PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review, I was happy to agree. Read on to find out what we thought of them.

Table of Contents

## PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review

With an RRP of £99, the PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones are definitely not cheap. I was sent two pairs of these headphones – one each for Sam and Syd. A Blue pair and a Pinky Purple pair. So Syd immediately claimed the blue pair as her own. The quality of the packaging is high, and I was impressed by the included carry case. That definitely makes transporting them between her Dad’s house and mine less challenging.

### What Puro Sound Labs Say

When researching for this PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review, I realised just how much technology is packed into these headphones…

Image Credit

The ANC switch means kids can listen clearly, even in loud environments… Without the need to increase the volume beyond safe sound listening levels. It’s almost as if the rest of the world is put on mute, when the headphones are put on. According to Puro, these headphones make daily noise and background sound up to 22 dB quieter. This is complemented by 82% noise isolation.

### What’s In The PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones Box

Image Credit

As well as the headphones, you also receive a hard carry case, instructions, charging cable and 3.5mm limiter audio cable. This is so handy for the devices which don’t support a wireless connection.

The headphones do need charging as soon as you receive them. So if you’re buying these as a gift, it’s worth opening and charing them before wrapping. Thankfully, the packaging allows this, so they will still look brand new when opened.

### My Thoughts

Honestly, I don’t understand all of the jargon but when she was wearing them… 8 year old Syd thought I was miming, rather than talking, when I was asking her what she wanted for lunch. That’s the most important bit of information in this PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review. They definitely cancel out external noise, so help kids concentrate on the task at hand.

The wireless range is 32 feet (or 9.75m if you prefer). This means Syd can keep her headphones on and walk away from her laptop to get a drink, without missing any of the audio from her class teacher.

With a battery life of up to 16 hours with audio cancelling activated, and 22 hours without, these headphones stand up well to daily life. I tend to charge them every other night at the moment, as she wears them for a good 4-6 hours a day. The included limiter audio cable means that even if the batteries do run out, Syd can use them via that.

When the headphones are charging, an orange light appears on the headphones. I did accidentally think they were charging once but the cable wasn’t in right. So make sure the light is on when you connect them.

### Syd’s Thoughts

Syd loves the blue pair, but isn’t a fan of the pink ones. (She hates pink though, so that’s no surprise). She says they are comfy to wear and the sound quality is great. She’s had them connected to her laptop and her iPad with ease.

It connects via bluetooth and according to the instructions… “The one-touch Bluetooth pairing with iPhone, Android, and other compatible devices makes for hassle-free listening”. All told, I think the PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review has shown that these are a great option for kids.

Finally, if you’re looking to spend less, but still want decent kids headphones, the PuroBasic Headphones are a great option, too. Let me know in the comments if you have anything to add to this PuroQuiet noise cancelling headphones review.

# Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Kids Headphones Review

## These noise-cancelling headphones for kids are a must buy for every parent

 

 Written by TJ Donegan, who has covered electronics, TVs, smartphones, parenting for 10+ years. 

 Tested by Julia MacDougall 

 April 15, 2019 

While there are a million things for parents to worry about these days, noise-induced hearing loss is real—and pretty scary. In our testing, we’ve shown that even the cheap earbuds that came with your phone are dangerous at full volume, especially for long periods of time.

- About the Puro PuroQuiet Noise Cancelling Headphones 
- What we like 
- What we didn’t like 
- Should You Buy Them? 
- Get the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Kids Headphones for $99.99 

### Pros

- Cuts ambient noise with no technical issues 
- Safe for up to 8 hours 
- Tangle-free 

### Cons

- Expensive for kids headphones 

With more kids using headphones with their phones, tablets, and game consoles, having headphones that protect their hearing is more important than ever. That’s where the Puro PuroQuiet Noise Cancelling Headphones come in, the latest in Puro’s excellent line of volume-limiting headphones designed for kids and young adults.

In our lab testing, we’ve proven that these headphones adhere to the recommended volume limits established by experts. We’ve also used them enough to know they sound great, they do an excellent job of cancelling ambient noise, and they’re comfortable for children or adults with smaller heads. 

Add it up and you have the best kids headphones we’ve tested to date. Though you can save some money by opting for the non-noise cancelling version, if you want volume-limiting headphones, we think Puro’s lineup is your best bet.

## About the Puro PuroQuiet Noise Cancelling Headphones

 Credit: Reviewed / Jackson Ruckar 

The PuroQuiet Kids Headphones are wireless, noise-cancelling, and volume-safe. 

PuroQuiet headphones come in two colors, blue and pink, and feature an on/over-ear design that will likely envelop the ears of young children but may only qualify as “on-ear headphones” for adults. Here are the specs from Puro Sound:

- Active Noise Cancellation 
- 85 dB(a) volume limiting
- Two integrated microphones for ANC and communication
- 82% noise isolation at 1kHz
- Up to 16 hours battery life with ANC, 22 hours without
- Bluetooth 4.0
- Premium audio wireless listening 
- Full compatibility with PC, Android and iPhone devices
- In the Box: USB charging cable, 3.5mm aux audio cable, travel case, user manual

The PuroQuiet headphones are designed to be “volume-limited” headphones, meaning they have a maximum volume output of—according to Puro—85dB(a). This is the level recommended by most experts for a maximum of eight hours per day.

The PuroQuiet headphones are designed to be “volume-limited” headphones, meaning they have a maximum volume near 85dB(a).

Most headphones are powered by the analog signal that comes through a standard headphone or aux jack. This determines how loud the headphones can get, and volume-limited headphones usually feature special technology that will reduce the power of this incoming signal to keep the volume beneath this safe threshold.

When used wirelessly, this isn’t a concern; the headphones power themselves so everything is controlled. The PuroQuiets are designed so that they will also be safe even when used wired up to a source (like an amp) that might power them to dangerous levels.

## What we like

There’s a lot about the PuroQuiet headphones to like. Right out of the box, it’s clear you’re getting a product that is built to a much higher standard than most of the competition. Most kids’ headphones are made of cheap-feeling plastic that is easy to break.

 Credit: Reviewed / Jackson Ruckar 

Puro's headphones all feature a simple design with padded earcups that are super comfortable for kids to wear. 

The PuroQuiets are made of mostly metal, with a sturdy adjustable headband and soft, plush earcups. The adjustable headband means they can easily fit a child as young as 3 and an adult, though if you have a large head circumference you may find them uncomfortable.

The sound quality on the headphones is actually quite good, which is not the case with most kids’ headphones I’ve used. Music and podcasts both sounded great, and the lower volume limits were still plenty loud for my needs.

In our lab tests, we found the headphones stuck closely to the recommended level of 85dB(a) at most, straying at times up to the 88dB(a) territory but not any further. Our tests also showed the noise cancelling was very effective, cutting down ambient noise by __. For some context, high-end noise-cancelling headphones like the Bose QuietComfort 35 cut ambient noise by __. 

Comfort-wise, it’s hard to gauge just how good the Puro headphones are (since they’re really best-suited to, well, kids) but they’re well-built, adjustable, and the earcups are very comfortable. We haven’t read any user complaints, so we think most kids will like these just fine.

## What we didn’t like

There are only a few things about the PuroQuiets that give us pause. The most obvious one is the price, with the noise-cancelling model having an MSRP of $199. Though noise-cancelling is a rare feature in the kids’ headphones space, there are certainly more affordable volume-limiting models out there. Puro’s own BT2200, which is also wireless but lacks active noise cancellation, has an MSRP of just $99.

 Credit: Reviewed / Jackson Ruckar 

The PuroQuiets are meant to be used wirelessly or wired, with a volume-limiting cable that can hook up to 3.5mm aux ports. 

Both models are typically on sale, though, with the PuroQuiet often dropping to $99 and the BT2200 around $69 or lower. That’s still pricey for a pair of kids’ headphones, but very reasonable for headphones in general—especially for this noise-cancelling model.

Otherwise, we just have a few concerns about the Puro design. The adjustable headband is great, but the headphones only fit in the travel case when the band is slid into its smallest setting. This means you have to re-adjust them every time you put them on.

In our lab tests, there were no major red flags—though there is some minimal distortion with mid-range and higher frequencies. It is there, but not something you’re going to notice or complain about frequently.

## Should You Buy Them?

The PuroQuiets are the best kids’ headphones we’ve ever tested, bar none. Forgetting the volume-limiting capabilities and the kid-friendly design for a moment, they’re just great headphones. They have good battery life, great noise-cancellation, excellent build quality, and a good overall sound profile with no major red flags. 

 Credit: Reviewed / Jackson Ruckar 

The PuroQuiets are available in a number of colors, but the bright, colorful styling should appeal to all kinds of kids. 

The only major hangup we would have is the price; most kids headphones cost between $20-40, while these go for around $100 on sale and have an MSRP of $200. They perform like $200 headphones, though, so deciding whether they’re worth the money is more about who you’re planning to give them to.

These cost more than most kids headphones, but they perform like $200 pairs we've tested.

If you just want a pair of headphones to protect your kids’ hearing, then a cheaper model may make more sense. Even if you like this design, the Puro BT2200—which frequently goes for closer to $70—is a good compromise that still gives you wireless capability and limits volume to safe levels.

Where the PuroQuiets stand out is active noise-cancellation. They’re excellent at it, and you just don’t get that with any other kids’ headphones we’ve tested. If your child prefers noise cancellation, or has sensory issues and may benefit from it, then these are a great alternative. They’re much cheaper on sale than the best from Bose and Sony, with a kid-friendly design that also limits volume to safe levels.

PuroQuiet Plus Review: $119 Noise-Cancelling Kids Headphones

# Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Noise-Cancelling Headphones Reviewed

 By Jerry Del Colliano Author's Reference AV System Last updated on October 27, 2026 Reading Time: 8 minutes 

Price: $ 119.00

There isn’t an audiophile out there who doesn’t have a story about how they have abused their hearing at one level or another. Car stereo systems are a likely historical venue for past auditory abuse. Workplace noise is another common one. For me, it was seeing Metallica on the … And Justice for All Tour at the Philadelphia Spectrum circa 1989. The funny part was that Metallica wasn’t as loud as the opening act, The Cult. Years later, for my 25 th birthday, I ended up meeting the band members from The Cult (and John Bonham’s widow and family) at a club in Hollywood and I told them just how loud they played. They couldn’t have been happier to hear the report all those years later. Realistically, it is a miracle that I have the hearing left that I do. Now that I am a father of two boys, I only hope to protect their hearing better than I did when I was their age. When I took my older son and his 13-year-old buddy to see the Grammy-winning surf-punk-metal act Turnstile at USC in 2025, I had them wear earplugs. When I took my four-year-old son to Maui, he needed a cool travel rig like his Dad. Listening to headphones too loudly (especially over long periods of time) is really bad for hearing. This is why I got him a pair of Puro headphones for the trip. 

The PuroQuiet Plus ($119 – buy at Amazon) from Puro Sound Labs is a pair of on-ear, Bluetooth, active noise-canceling headphones made specifically for kids. Adults know better than to blow their hearing out, but kids would be well-served being more protected, and that is the stated goal of Puro with these headphones. How do they work? How do they sound? Are they worth it? That’s what we are here to explore.

Rainbow colors for the Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Plus kids headphones.

## What Makes the PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Headphones So Special?

- The PuroQuiet Plus headphones limit output volume to 85 dB. Puro does this with DSP (digital signal processing) rather than a resistor in a cable, and the idea is that the kid never really “hits a wall” on the volume knob. 85 dB is the number you will see referenced in hearing-safety guidelines for long listening sessions, and that is the whole point of these headphones. Your kid can’t override it, and neither can their friend who knows how to get into the settings on the iPad or other kid-hackable devices. 
- The active noise cancellation reduces up to 22 dB of outside noise. This is a design concept that makes the volume limit actually work in the real world. Without ANC, a kid on an airplane or a school bus might realistically push the volume up to compete with the background noise. With a little ANC, the need is less. Is it Sony- or Bose-level ANC? No, and Puro doesn’t claim that this is what they deliver, but it really helps without creating too much of an ANC bubble for the kids. 
- The battery life on the PuroQuiet Plus is rated at 35 hours with ANC off and 23 hours with ANC on. By today’s standards, that isn’t the longest battery life but it is realistically quite a long time. Also, if a pair of Puros were to be left to drain to no battery – you can recharge them via USB-C very quickly. A 10-to-15-minute charge gives you lots and lots of additional listening time. 
- There is a wired connection option with a volume-limiting cable included. If the battery does run out, or you are on an airplane with a seatback screen, the included 3.5mm cable still keeps the volume limit in place. This option is nice to have, but personally not one that I want from a wireless pair of headphones. 
- Puro includes a daisy-chain cable, which is really thoughtful. This allows two sets of headphones to share one audio source. Anybody who has had two kids fighting over one iPad in the back of a car on a road trip understands the value of this little cable.
- The PuroQuiet Plus comes with a pretty nicely appointed hard-shell carrying case. I abuse the hell out of my wireless headphones, because I refuse to use such a case (all my headphones have them), yet for some reason, we always use the case for the Puros, which are still in near mint condition thanks to the case and careful attention. 
- The PuroQuiet Plus uses a 40mm dynamic driver and is reported at 20 Hz to 20 kHz with less than one percent THD. That’s a pretty big driver for a small ear cup and some pretty good frequency range performance.
- There is a built-in microphone for online school, video calls and gaming. My older son uses ROG (Republic of Gaming) headphones with a robust microphone for collaborating while playing Roblox, Fortnite and other video games. My little guy doesn’t have those needs, but the microphone functionality is a nice plus. 
- The vibrant colors offered are perfect for kids. Teal, dark blue, light pink and purple are on Puro’s site right now. My son’s pair is in the teal finish. 

Puro Sound Labs PuroQuiet Plus worn by Jerry’s youngest son.

## Why Should You Care About the PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Headphones?

At FutureAudiophile.com, we talk a lot about how to grow the hobby with the next generation of music lovers. If you are basically hard of hearing by the time you are in high school, then you don’t really need a pair of $20,000 monoblock power amps years down the road. As a parent, protecting my kids’ hearing is just me doing my job. As an audiophile and publisher, introducing the hobby to younger people is my stated goal in the mission statement of this publication. Protecting their hearing from an early age seems really reasonable to me and likely for the young people that you know in your world, thus why I am so fond of their design philosophy of hearing protection for kids. 

## Some Things You Might Not Like About the PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Headphones

- The PuroQuiet Plus is an on-ear design, not over-the-ear. On-ear headphones are lighter and better-sized for smaller heads, but they don’t seal out sound as well as over-the-ear cups, and some kids will find the clamping force a bit much on long sessions, but allowing a little external sound to leak in has a safety upside that I also like. I often mention in my over-the-ear, ANC headphone reviews that you want to be careful when walking down the street with the ANC on, as you could get run over in the crosswalk if you are not careful. Kids are even more susceptible. 
- The ANC is pretty good, but it is not flagship-level. If you are comparing these to your own Sony or Bose headphones (at a much higher price), you can hear the difference, but there is a reason for this, which we’ve already explained. 
- The 85 dB limit is fixed. It would be cool to adjust the volume limits, but that is by no means a deal-breaker.
- There is no Puro app for these headphones. No EQ and no firmware updates from your phone, as well as no parental dashboard. Your kids might expect an app but, at these prices, I think I can live without one and not be too bummed out. 

## Listening to the PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Headphones

This was a tricky and imperfect evolution, mainly because I have a physically big head (leave my bloated ego out of this …) and these PuroQuiet Plus headphones are designed for kids with significantly smaller heads. I think I got a good feel for how they sound, but it important to disclose that pure audiophile performance isn’t the driving force as to why you would make this investment. Hearing protection is the driving force for why you throw a few pairs of these into your Amazon cart at the holidays and make some holiday dreams come true for the kids in your life. 

“Superstition” from Stevie Wonder’s Talking Book album is a 1972 R&B classic, as well as a fantastically catchy audiophile demo track. The Bob Margouleff-produced song is layered with horns and other tasty instrumentation, and that came across very nicely when listening to the PuroQuiet Plus headphones. The bass wasn’t hitting subsonic depths (it never does on headphones like this), but it sounded groovy and fun. The horns sounded warm, rich and layered. I was impressed. 

In looking for a fun, kid-friendly jam, I cued up the Bruno Mars/Mark Ronson song “Uptown Funk,” which my younger son thinks is just great. I liked the PuroQuiet Plus headphones’ ability to present depth on the syncopated call-and-response background vocals. The horns were even more poppy and vibrant on this track than on “Superstition,” which is likely the result of the modern recording. The bass guitar felt lit. It hit deep notes, but the articulated bass chops were tasty-sounding, too. If you can’t groove to this song, then something might be wrong with you.

My favorite demo in the modern era is Beyoncé’s cover of “Blackbird,” which brings the songwriting of Lennon and McCartney to the female voice of our generation with a modern, reinvented production. It is pure audiophile gold for any system. On the PuroQuiet Plus headphones, Beyoncé’s voice sounded warm and engaging. Again, the layering and depth was well-presented (even with the headphones jammed on my head, which is a me problem, not a Puro problem), well beyond my expectations for headphones at this price point, let alone ones with all of the other thoughtful features. 

## Will the PuroQuiet Plus Kids’ Headphones Hold Their Value?

Absolutely not. Kids will beat the snot out of these headphones and they cost $119, thus you are recycling or tossing them when your kids are done. The best hope would be that you could gift or reuse the PuroQuiet Plus headphones again with another kid, but forget resale value, as that is just an unreasonable expectation with this value proposition and with such a low retail price.

The BuddyPhones Cosmos+ ($99.99) is the most direct competitor. They are ov
